easy_geo_chapter_1_desc: Learn simple concepts about our planet, waters, and landforms.
easy_geo_1_desc: It is not safe to look directly at the Sun, even during an eclipse. Its light can damage your eyes.
easy_geo_1_question: How do we protect our eyes when we want to observe a solar eclipse?
easy_geo_1_hint: It is also known as the Blue Planet.
easy_geo_2_desc: Throughout the day, the Sun appears to move across the sky from east to west.
easy_geo_2_question: Does that mean the Sun revolves around the Earth?
easy_geo_2_hint: Think about why Earth looks blue when seen from space.
easy_geo_3_desc: Sunlight looks white, but it is made up of many colors. When light passes through water droplets, the colors can separate and become visible.
easy_geo_3_question: What can we sometimes see when it rains and, at the same time, the Sun is shining?
easy_geo_3_hint: It is the opposite direction of where the Sun sets (West).
easy_geo_4_desc: A year is the time a planet needs to make a complete journey around the Sun. Each planet has its own "year"
easy_geo_4_question: Planets farther from the Sun take longer to orbit it
easy_geo_4_hint: Europe is the continent adjacent to Asia and Africa.
easy_geo_5_desc: Many planets have natural satellites orbiting them. Earth has the Moon, and some planets have a great many satellites. But there are also planets that have none at all
easy_geo_5_question: Group the planets into the appropriate category
easy_geo_5_hint: Think about where you can swim and where you can hike on foot.
easy_geo_6_desc: When a comet approaches the Sun, the heat causes some of its ice to turn into gas and release dust. The solar wind helps push some of this material away from the Sun
easy_geo_6_question: What contributes to the formation and orientation of a comet's tail?
easy_geo_6_op_2: The Sun and the solar wind
easy_geo_6_hint: It is the sea located to the east of Romania.
easy_geo_7_desc: Earth attracts objects due to a force called gravity. It keeps us on the ground and causes objects we drop to fall
easy_geo_7_question: If you drop a ball from your hand, gravity pulls it toward the Earth?
easy_geo_7_hint: Tall pine trees grow in the mountains, home to bears, wolves, and deer.
easy_geo_8_question: Match each celestial body with the correct description
easy_geo_8_right_3: It rotates almost lying on its side
easy_geo_8_hint: A compass has a needle that always points North.
easy_geo_9_question: Order the planets from the closest to the Sun to the farthest
easy_geo_9_hint: Plains are flat and low, while mountains reach up into the clouds.
easy_geo_10_desc: In about a month, the Moon passes through several phases. Sometimes we see it whole, other times only half, or as a crescent
easy_geo_10_question: Why does the Moon seem to change its shape?
easy_geo_10_op_1: The Moon really changes its shape
easy_geo_10_op_2: We see different portions of its sunlit side
easy_geo_10_op_3: Clouds cover parts of the Moon
easy_geo_10_hint: It is the largest city in the country and is home to the Palace of Parliament.
easy_geo_10_op_4: The Earth's shadow covers it every night
